source_issues.finding: The displayed Matrix class lacks __matmul__, so the exercise @ expression fails for that copied excerpt; the complete code/matrices.py explicitly defines __matmul__ at lines 106–107. Complete implementation defect must not be claimed.
Universal image-as-matrix, every-layer-as-matrix-transformation and every-dense-layer-as-ReLU claims are introductory overgeneralizations. Source scope retained.

Broadcasting example correctly repeats [10,20,30] across rows, but source prose omits right-aligned equal-or-one compatibility and singleton-axis expansion. Chinese does not strengthen or silently fix it.

Displayed snippets lack shape and nonempty guards; zip may truncate; determinant/inverse need square/2x2 constraints. Exact det==0 is not a robust near-singularity test. Complete implementation has separate checks and abs(det)<1e-10, which is a numerical threshold, not an algebraic definition of singularity.
Orders-of-magnitude/100x claims are unbenchmarked and BLAS dispatch depends on dtype/backend/size. Preserved 100x does not indicate this review measured speed.
Zero vector has no direction; determinant is signed scaling of a square-matrix transformation and inverse/determinant equivalence presumes square matrices. Simplifications are already in source.
